parameters.label: Configuration source
parameters.description: inherit reads the original entry when present; own reads this entry. Switching does not copy values.

parameters.label: Toggle Key
parameters.description: Input action name used to hide or show the message window on Scene_Map. none disables the shortcut.
parameters.context: Use a suggested action such as tab or shift; other strings require a matching RPG Maker Input mapping. The shortcut works during message input or an active choice, number-input or item-selection window. Visibility changes are unavailable in battle and other scenes or while the message window forbids toggling. Confirm or touch can restore a hidden message; hiding does not erase its contents. Enable Coreto_4_MessageVisibility 0.1.0 with message-visibility install after its optional providers/consumers have been arranged; the bundle must already be delivered. install selects this provider instead of VisuMZ_4_MessageVisibility and preserves other provider selections. Restart the game after configuration changes. Place this plugin after any active Core/Message providers and Picture Choices, VN Picture Busts, Choice Common Events, Extended Message Function, Animated Message Text Effects, Attached Pictures and Event Title Scene. Core Engine and Message Core are optional; supported versions are Coreto_0_CoreEngine 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_0_CoreEngine 1.90 and Coreto_1_MessageCore 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_1_MessageCore 1.57, with at most one provider in each pair. The CLI edits js/plugins.js for the next game boot; it does not change an already running game. parameters reset and missing native values use this entry's published default. parameters get reports the effective value; message-visibility api describe CORETO-CONFIG-SOURCE explains inherit/own. Action names are case-sensitive. With native mappings, tab is Tab, shift is Shift/gamepad X, control is Ctrl or Alt, pageup is Page Up/Q/gamepad LB, and pagedown is Page Down/W/gamepad RB; none disables this shortcut. Unknown or empty names have no shortcut unless mapped by another plugin. Restoring consumes the input without advancing text or confirming a choice; hidden selectors can also restore through cursor/confirm/cancel input. Picture clicks are blocked while hidden, and Picture Choices windows hidden by PC-T-HIDE stay hidden when the message is restored. Visibility is window-instance state, not saved game configuration; recreating the scene starts with normal window visibility. Evented title maps are excluded: this feature requires the exact Scene_Map constructor. If the shortcut overlaps Extended Message auto-forward, visibility handling takes precedence.

parameters.label: Common Event on Show
parameters.description: Common Event ID to launch when the message window actually changes from hidden to visible on Scene_Map. Select its ID from Database > Common Events; 0 disables this callback.
parameters.context: Requires a Message provider implementing launchMessageCommonEvent. With Coreto_1_MessageCore, an absent Common Event ID is ignored and a separate interpreter runs the event alongside map events. Repeating show while already visible, battle/other scenes, and forbidden toggles do not launch it. The callback is not the initial opening of every message. The CLI edits js/plugins.js for the next game boot; it does not change an already running game. parameters reset and missing native values use this entry's published default. parameters get reports the effective value; message-visibility api describe CORETO-CONFIG-SOURCE explains inherit/own. See message-visibility api describe MV-P-ToggleKey:str for provider activation, scene restrictions and visibility lifecycle. Enable Coreto_1_MessageCore 0.1.0 (with its Coreto_0_CoreEngine dependency) or VisuMZ_1_MessageCore 1.57 before Message Visibility for this callback. The event runs without blocking the map; opposite/repeated visibility changes may leave earlier events running. With Coreto Message, completed interpreters are removed and map setup clears pending message interpreters; save/load preserves serialized map interpreters. Use an existing Common Event database ID from data/CommonEvents.json. The CLI stores an integer; it does not execute or create that event.

parameters.context: Requires a Message provider implementing launchMessageCommonEvent. Repeating hide while already hidden, battle/other scenes, and forbidden toggles do not launch it. Closing a message normally does not trigger this callback. With Coreto Message, completed interpreters are removed and map setup clears pending message interpreters; save/load preserves serialized map interpreters. parameters.label: Button Name
parameters.description: Text of the hide button in the Extended Message Function button console beside the message window.
parameters.context: To display this button, enable Coreto_2_ExtMessageFunc before this plugin, include hide in its Buttons.List, and show the button console on Scene_Map. Its visibility also follows the console's message-specific hiding and auto-size settings. This parameter only changes the label; it does not create a button without the console, change the toggle key, or enable visibility changes outside Scene_Map. The CLI edits js/plugins.js for the next game boot; it does not change an already running game. parameters reset and missing native values use this entry's published default. parameters get reports the effective value; message-visibility api describe CORETO-CONFIG-SOURCE explains inherit/own. See message-visibility api describe MV-P-ToggleKey:str for provider activation, scene restrictions and visibility lifecycle. Query ext-message api describe EXT-M-016 for Buttons.List, EXT-M-015 for console layout/ShowDefault, and EXT-M-003 for the runtime show command. The label is plain drawText text, not a filename or text-code expression; an empty string leaves the button unlabeled rather than removing it. Include the exact hide token in the list. Extended Message Function 0.1.0 must be active before Message Visibility; neither label changes nor CLI writes redraw an existing runtime console.
